annotations.title: Add or change a Proactive Messages rule

description: Add a Proactive Messages rule, or change one (pass rule_id from list_proactive_messages; fields you leave out keep their value). The chatbot then writes first, live for every visitor at once, when the trigger happens. For a general greeting bubble shown to everyone, use update_widget_settings instead. Pro and Enterprise only. A fixed text shows at once and costs nothing; an AI rule spends one AI reply each time it shows. On phones the message always shows in a bubble. For trigger_type event, the website must send the event in its code: window.Asyntai = window.Asyntai || {}; (window.Asyntai.events = window.Asyntai.events || []).push({ name: 'added_to_cart', data: { product: 'Running shoes' } });

display.description: bubble: a bubble above the chat button. open: the chat opens with the message (on phones it is always a bubble).

enabled.description: Whether the rule is on. New rules are on.

frequency.description: session: once per visit. visitor: once per visitor. always: every time (never twice within 30 seconds).

message_mode.description: fixed: the visitor sees message_text exactly. ai: message_text is an instruction and the AI writes the message in the visitor's language.

message_text.description: The fixed text, or the instruction for the AI.

name.description: Name only the owner sees, to find the rule in the list.

rule_id.description: Id of the rule to change, from list_proactive_messages. Omit to add a new rule.

translations.description: Fixed text only: language code to translated text, for example {"de": "...", "cs": "..."}. Each visitor sees the text of their browser language, and the main text when there is none. Replaces the whole set.

trigger_type.description: When the chatbot writes: event (the website code sends an event name), click (a click on a CSS selector), url (the page address contains a text) or time (seconds on the page).

trigger_value.description: The event name (for example added_to_cart), the CSS selector (for example #copy-code), the text in the page address (for example /pricing) or the number of seconds (for example 30).

website_id.description: Numeric id of the website, from list_websites. Omit to use the account's primary website.
